label: dense copy-phase feature, strongest when outputting j
explanation: Dense feature: active on 43% of all steps and in over 99% of sequences. It is broadly a copy-phase feature. Steps after <DEL> fire 67% of the time and hold 78% of activation mass (dev F1 0.67, mass recall 0.78). During the original phase it fires less often (25%); the rate is highest at t=0-1 and at the last original positions before <DEL>, and lowest in the middle of the sequence. On the <DEL> step itself it fires 33% of the time. Within the copy phase the rate peaks at recall_idx 1-4 (about 0.70) and declines slowly toward the end. Magnitude depends on the token being output: the top activations are almost all steps outputting j (out_tok j is active 87% of the time but covers only 5% of mass), followed by 1, k, m, t and p. Limiting to that high-rate output set raises precision to 0.81 but drops recall to 0.26. About 33% of copy steps are inactive, with no simple token or position rule explaining which ones. Adding early-original-phase positions raises mass recall (0.86-0.91) but lowers precision. The feature has no clear preference for in_tok, L or digit count.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: j, 1, p, m; input phase: x, l, s, i; delimiter step: ) and the previous input (most: l, x, g, i, 2, 3; least: 0, t, a, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=3 & t=4, L=4 & t=5.
